svg.title: Multiple Recovery Paths in a Lesioned Transformer
svg.desc: A0 portrait BlackboxNLP 2026 scientific conference poster.

rect.style: stroke: none; stroke-linecap: butt; stroke-width: 1; fill: rgb(100%,100%,100%); fill-rule: evenodd;

g.text: Multiple Recovery Paths in a Lesioned Transformer
A pretrained BERT encoder and a learned linear readout classify each word into one of 17 part-of-speech categories. A
large immediate accuracy drop after removing a learned sparse, task-sufficient configuration establishes necessity only
for that fixed routing and readout. Allowing the residual model to adapt asks a second question: can performance return
through another route, and must that recovery restore the original hidden-state representation?

rect.style: stroke: none; stroke-linecap: butt; stroke-width: 1; fill: rgb(91%,94%,97%); fill-rule: evenodd;

g.text: High POS accuracy can return without
Learn a sparse task-sufficient route, hold the lesion fixed, then vary what can adapt

Schematic: connections illustrate parameter status, not measured activation flow.
Five-seed recovery preserves the same ordering

g.text: Bars are means across five independent full-pipeline seeds; circles are individual runs and short lines
show the observed range, not confidence intervals. The displayed gate-only result is the
density-promoting variant. Mask-only recovery is visibly more seed-sensitive than readout, joint, or
Performance and return to the core representation diverge

g.text: Linear centered kernel alignment (CKA) measures hidden-state similarity, not recovered circuitry.
Primary-seed endpoints are shown because matching representations are available for that run.
Readout-only stays at the damaged model's CKA by construction while accuracy rises from 16.82% to
A new readout extracts useful POS information from the same damaged representation
